sources.title: Yakama Nation Museum: Yakama History
sources.note: Indexed original read in full; direct open returned 400. Reproducible query: site.yakamamuseum.com/home-history.php "Tribal Council" "1944". Identity, distinct tribes before 1855, Mool-mool, 1944 council and resolutions T-053-94/T-172-99.

sources.title: Treaty with the Yakima, 1855: primary text
sources.note: Direct text read: heading, preamble and Articles 1, 2, 3 and 5. Signing, ratification and proclamation distinguished; promises not treated as delivered services.

sources.title: Meyer Resources for CRITFC: Tribal Circumstances and Impacts, 1999
sources.note: Direct PDF: printed pp. 135 to 136, PDF indices 141 to 142, Table 15 based on Helen Schuster and Florence L. Aguilar memorandum of May 29, 1995. Seasonal account is a reconstruction; no modeled annual fish-consumption quantities adopted.

sources.title: Jeanne M. Welch: Kamiakin’s Gardens, National Register nomination, 1976
sources.note: Direct PDF, Section 8 continuation pp. 2 to 4, PDF indices 4 to 6. Specific garden crops, ditch and 1855 to 1858 events checked; obsolete civilizing rhetoric and erroneous characterization of other tribes rejected.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Yakama basket 22/5134
sources.note: Direct catalog Culture/People, materials, techniques and collection history. Donated 1957; manufacture date and earlier collecting history unknown.

sources.title: Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission: Celilo Falls
sources.note: Direct page, opening historical account, 1957 inundation and Raymond Matheny’s 1952 photographic notes. Intertribal fishing place, not exclusively Yakama.

sources.title: Yakama Nation Ichishkíin Sɨ́nwit Language Program: Materials & Videos
sources.note: Direct modern community page: exact bilingual Life is Good heading and creator/recording credits; nursing, babyboards, diapering, baby kind talk and handwashing resources. The link labelled storybook PDF resolves to YouTube; witness here is the printed page heading, not an inspected PDF.

sources.title: Yakama Nation: Mid-Columbia Coho Restoration Program Master Plan, 2017
sources.note: Direct PDF printed p. 78 / PDF index 89, Section 4.1, and Table 3-1 printed p. 63 / PDF index 74. Results distinguished from long-term goals.

sources.title: Douglas Veltre for APIA: Unangax̂ History
sources.note: Direct full text: Population and Territory, Russian Period, Pribilof Islands, World War II. No claim that Pribilof or Commander Islands were settled in 1492; no present-day speaker counts copied from undated historical account.

sources.title: National Park Service: Anangula National Historic Landmark
sources.note: Direct page: distinct Core and Blade site around 9,000 years old versus younger village. Ancient Tool Factory and A Bygone Aleutian Village sections. No claim that younger house ruins date to 9,000 years ago.

sources.title: National Park Service: Unangax̂ History and Culture
sources.note: Direct page, updated August 5, 2024. Family Unit, Unangax̂ Homes and Transportation, Tools, and Clothes. Family description bounded to historical account; no claim of universal contemporary household practice.

sources.title: Smithsonian: Attu gut parka, collected 1891 to 1898
sources.note: Indexed original read in full with query "Gut Parka Made Of Seal Intestines" Smithsonian. Direct page internal error. Object metadata and 2003 discussions with Mary N. Bourdukofsky, Vlass Shabolin, Maria Turnpaugh and Daria Dirks. Collection date not manufacture date; accession 1943 not used as object date.

sources.title: National Park Service: Unangax̂ Evacuation and Internment
sources.note: Direct text: 881 people from nine villages, Atka burning, camp facilities and self-help; Attu Japanese captivity identified separately in linked publication description. No conflicting death totals adopted.

sources.title: University of Alaska Fairbanks: Unangam Tunuu / Aleut
sources.note: Direct ANLC page: 1824 Veniaminov collaboration, Bergsland/Dirks work, 1994 dictionary and 1997 grammar. Population and speaker figures not reused as current statistics.

sources.title: Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association: Food Sovereignty Program
sources.note: Direct modern community page headings: English Subsistence is sustenance for the life; Eastern/Qagaadan Tunuu Qaqamiiĝux̂ qalgadam ukulganaa ngiin ugutaasakun. English reproduced exactly rather than silently improving unusual wording.

sources.title: CDC: Traditional Foods in Native America, Part V
sources.note: Direct PDF printed pp. 39 to 42 / PDF indices 39 to 42. APIA Head Start Traditional Foods Preschool Curriculum; named cultural mentors, 2016 development, six units, recipes and family letters.

sources.title: Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association: Cultural Heritage Department
sources.note: Direct page: preservation of languages, practices, archaeological/historical places and objects; education for new generations; department formed in 1998.

batchIdentityNotes.recommendation: Share one phased Yakama narrative; retain distinct imported date intervals and polygons. Do not absorb independently indexed constituent or neighboring peoples.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: Decoded Yakima 1530 feature is centered on the Yakima Valley, bbox [-121.5102,45.7139,-118.9506,47.0166], indexed 1530 to 1783. Yakama world1492 is a broader regional polygon, bbox [-121.8810,45.5976,-117.8022,48.4815], indexed 1492 to 1500. These are not equal geometries. Museum explicitly establishes Yakima/Yakama spelling connection through T-053-94 and distinguishes the pre-1855 tribes from the later fourteen-tribe confederation. Public opening explains both geographic and political limits.

batchIdentityNotes.recommendation: Distinct living Unangax̂ people, no merged aliases. Preserve imported 1492 to 1500 as coverage only.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: Decoded world1492 MultiPolygon bbox [-168.5555,53.2358,-159.9766,56.1680] covers eastern Aleutians/Alaska Peninsula portion, not full Aleutian chain. APIA Population and Territory gives western Alaska Peninsula, Shumagins and Aleutians to Attu; Pribilofs likely not settled until Russian colonial period and Commanders unpopulated in 1741. Opening explicitly warns partial outline; later Attu and Pribilof narratives intentionally broader than geometry.
